title: Logger level changes leak between tests
reasoning: The proxy-method test sets the shared stdlib logger named 'test' to WARNING without restoring its level. The autouse fixture resets only structlog. If the basic logging test runs afterward, caplog.at_level(DEBUG) changes the root logger's level, but the named logger still rejects DEBUG and INFO records. This makes results depend on test order.
reproduction: Run test_adapter_logger_methods followed by test_basic_logging_without_kwargs in the same pytest process using their fully qualified node IDs.
recommendation: Snapshot and restore the levels of named loggers modified by these tests, and establish the required level explicitly for each capture scenario.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The default declaration order runs basic logging before the test that leaves WARNING set; subsequent scenarios often manually set DEBUG, masking the leak.
suggestedRegressionTest: Verify that logging tests preserve preexisting named-logger levels and that capture scenarios pass independently of preceding logger configuration.

history.reasoning: Current tests/logging_test.py supports the intended repair: reset_logging_state at lines 18–31 snapshots and restores test/test1/test2 logger levels; basic logging at lines 37–53 explicitly captures the named logger at DEBUG. The proxy-method test still sets WARNING at lines 242–256, but now has fixture cleanup. A capture-independence scenario also exists. No linked patch attempts were supplied.
